subject: ParcelIQ onboarding: pricing thresholds, migration credits, and SLA
messages:
From: Caroline Turner <caroline@parceliq.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Initial pricing ask and competing offer

Ben —

Thanks for the intro last week. Procurement here — we received a competing commercial from another inference vendor and wanted to give Redwood a chance to respond before we move to a shortlist. High level: they proposed a blended token rate with a steeper volume discount and a 3-month onboarding credit (to offset migration cost). We care most about: predictable per-token cost at scale, latency SLOs for 99p/99.9p, and a migration window with engineering support.

Quick context: ParcelIQ is planning a production rollout (search + chat) for Q4 and expects ~1B tokens/month after ramp. The commercial we received is below. Can you confirm whether Redwood can match/structure something comparable, and also outline any non-price considerations (migration assistance, runtime compatibility, KV/cache persistence during cutover)?

Competing commercial (redacted):
- 0–250M tokens/month: $0.00025/token
- 250M–1B: $0.00016/token
- >1B: $0.00011/token
- 3-month onboarding credit equal to 30% of the first quarter run-rate
- 99p latency SLO with penalty credits

We attached the PDF we received. Open to a quick call this week to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Caroline Turner
Head of Procurement, ParcelIQ
caroline@parceliq.com

[attachment: parceliq-rival-offer.pdf (pdf, 312KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Turner <caroline@parceliq.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing ask and competing offer

Caroline —

Appreciate the transparency and the PDF. Short answer: we can put together a competitive offer and a migration assistance package that focuses on two things you highlighted — unit economics at scale and low-risk cutover. High-level thoughts (so we can align before a call):

1) Pricing bands: we can propose a banded rate structure that narrows on 250M and 1B thresholds. I don't expect us to match the initial low-of-0.00011 at >1B immediately, but we can provide a stepped rebate guarantee tied to observed post-cutover consumption.

2) Onboarding credits: instead of a straight credit of X% of run-rate, we often offer a hybrid: a time-boxed credit (e.g., 3 months of credits) plus a committed engineering days bucket for integration (we'll staff an SRE + solutions engineer during the cutover window).

3) SLA/penalties: we have standard tiered SLOs; for deals of this size we can include financial backstop that mirrors yours for the 99p target (subject to mutually agreed metrics).

4) Technical migration: Redwood supports KV-prefetch and prefix cache export/import to reduce cold-start costs in the cutover. We'll also provide a migration checklist and a temporary dual-write pattern during the transition if you want seamless rollback.

Next steps: can your team do Wed 10–11am PT for a 30-min sync? I'll bring laura (pricing) and Marissa (solutions) to run the econ and technical assumptions. Please attach the competitor quote and any SOC/attestation requirements you need for procurement.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

[signature]

From: Procurement Team <procurement@parceliq.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Caroline Turner <caroline@parceliq.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing ask and competing offer

Ben / team —

Thanks — Wed 10am PT works. A few clarifications ahead of the call so we can be efficient:

- The competitor price is firm in the quote, and they included a clause that the >1B rate is conditional on a 12-month commitment at that band.
- ParcelIQ is open to a stepped guarantee (as you suggested), but procurement prefers an explicit credit schedule rather than case-by-case rebates.
- We will require at least 20 engineering days of vendor-provided migration support (SRE + solutions) and a named SLT contact for escalation in first 90 days.
- Attachment: our redlines doc (PDF converted to docx) — see "redlines-v1.docx". The legal team also flagged two items: data retention window clarity and SLA credit calculations.

On the call please be prepared to:
- Present a deterministic pricing table (per-band rates, how they change at thresholds)
- Confirm the onboarding credit mechanics (credit amount, how applied to invoices)
- Walk through the migration plan and the 20 engineering days scope (deliverables, travel if needed)
- Point to the SLA language and how 99p is measured (prod vs synthetic).

Call invite attached. 

Thanks,
ParcelIQ Procurement

[attachment: redlines-v1.docx (docx, 48KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Turner <caroline@parceliq.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@parceliq.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing ask and competing offer

Caroline / Procurement —

Appreciate the clarity — after the call we aligned internally and prepared a clear counterproposal (summary below). Putting the detailed commercial and the migration checklist in the DocLink and attachments.

Summary commercial (proposal):
- Banded unit price (USD/token):
  - 0–250M: $0.00026
  - 250M–1B: $0.00015
  - >1B: $0.00012
- Commitment options:
  - 12-month commitment: applies the above bands + 12% rebate applied quarterly if ramp targets met
  - No-commit pilot: month-to-month at a 5% premium to banded pricing, with no rebate
- Onboarding credit: 3 months of credits capped at 25% of projected first quarter run-rate OR 20 engineering days (whichever provides greater migration value). Engineering days include 2 onsite days if desired (travel budget included).
- SLA: 99p measured on production traffic over rolling 30-day windows. Redwood will include 1:1 credit parity with the competitor for any verified breaches (subject to metric definitions in contract).
- Migration support: named solutions lead (Marissa) + SRE on-call for 90 days after cutover. Detailed migration-checklist attached.

Commercial attachments & links:
- migration-checklist.xlsx (scope, milestones, rollback plan)
- redlines-v1.docx (we reviewed your notes and added clarifying language on retention and credits)
- DocuSign link to commercial Term Sheet: https://www.docusign.com/PIQ-3421-sign

We view the >1B band as achievable within 6 months post-cutover with the commitment option. If ParcelIQ can confirm a 12-month step commitment, we will extend the >1B target rate to $0.00011 after successful ramp validation and apply the 12% rebate. This gives you the low-end pricing you saw with the competitor while preserving runway for both teams.

Next steps:
- If this looks acceptable, I'll send the redline-ready term sheet via DocuSign and loop legal.
- If Procurement prefers a deterministic credit schedule instead of the hybrid credit/days approach, we can convert the engineering-days component into an equivalent cash credit (we put a suggested schedule in the attached sheet).

Let us know by EOD Monday and we'll prepare the signature packet and schedule a focused legal handoff.

Thanks — look forward to working together,
Ben
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
